what_it_does: A modern graphics chip (GPU) is divided internally into many small worker clusters called sub-cores, each with its own set of arithmetic units (the circuits that do the actual multiplication and addition). To save power, these sub-cores are walled off from each other, so if one sub-core's arithmetic unit is sitting idle waiting for a result, a neighboring sub-core's idle arithmetic unit cannot be borrowed — compute capacity is wasted. ACRS adds a thin coordination layer that watches for stalled instructions and quietly reroutes them to a free arithmetic unit in an adjacent sub-core, then routes the result back. Two small hardware modules handle the rerouting so the change does not require redesigning the whole chip. The paper claims this recovers meaningful compute capacity that is currently thrown away, though the exact workload coverage is not detailed in the abstract.
